title: Ethiopian Garlic Butter Sauce
localName: ቅቤ ነጭ ሽንኩርት — Qibe Nech Shinkurt
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Garlic Butter Sauce — kibbeh with abundant sliced garlic slowly cooked until the garlic is golden and fragrant, with a squeeze of lemon. The sauce used over grilled fish, tibs, and injera — kibbeh transformed by garlic into something greater.
longDesc: Ethiopian garlic butter sauce takes kibbeh as its base and enriches it with slowly cooked golden garlic — the garlic caramelises into the kibbeh fat, producing a sauce of extraordinary fragrance and depth used across Ethiopian grilling and fish preparations.
ingredients: ¼ cup fresh coriander or parsley
steps: Add sliced garlic. Cook slowly — 5—6 minutes until golden.
Do not rush — garlic must be golden, not burnt.
Pour over fish, tibs, or use as a dipping sauce.
chefTips: Sliced garlic, not minced — it caramelises more evenly.
The sizzle when lemon hits the hot kibbeh emulsifies them slightly.
Pour immediately — this sauce is best the moment it is made.
cookingScience: See ETH089 for sliced garlic caramelisation science. The lemon juice added to the hot kibbeh creates a temporary emulsion — the citric acid and water of the lemon partially emulsify into the fat, creating a less oily, more unified sauce.
servedWith: As a dipping sauce for injera
reheating: Can be remelted but loses freshness.
healthBenefits: Garlic allicin — powerfully antimicrobial and antioxidant.
culturalNote: Ethiopian garlic butter sauce is the modern restaurant's finishing touch — the sauce that arrives at the table still sizzling, poured over grilled fish by the server, filling the restaurant with the smell of golden garlic in kibbeh.
